action: GMO Pepabo advises changing the same password on other services, watching for suspicious emails, SMS and calls (it says it does not ask for passwords or card details), and contacting its support desk about any unrecognised login.
date_note: The page gives 27 November as the disclosure day; the company detected the suspicious downloads on 24 November.
exec: GMO Pepabo's notice gives 516,564 affected Lolipop! customer records.
geo_basis: country (company location not stated in the source)
plain: GMO Pepabo says customer data from its Lolipop! hosting services was taken after unauthorized access to its internal systems. Its notice gives 516,564 affected records. Some passwords were included; card and bank data were not.

sources.name: GMO Pepabo: notice on unauthorized access and customer data leak (Lolipop!), 27 Nov 2026
INTERNET Watch: Lolipop! plaintext password information leaked, 516,564 customer records possibly leaked

summary: GMO Pepabo says it detected suspicious data downloads on 24 November in the audit logs of its data analysis platform, after unauthorized access to its internal systems. Its notice gives 516,564 as the number of affected records. Names, postal codes, prefectures and email addresses are included, plus some passwords; credit card and bank account data are not.
title: GMO Pepabo says Lolipop! customer data was taken after unauthorized access to internal systems; 516,564 records affected so far
